(3) ⚠️ **The gate first went green with its behavioural half SILENTLY SKIPPED.** "Mark Paid" is a **two-step** control — `[data-pay]` expands the rep's row and only then are `[data-paynet]`/`[data-payfull]` rendered — so the one-step click found nothing, printed a note, and passed on the source checks alone. Fixed by clicking through both steps **and by making an unreachable screen a FAILURE rather than a note**: a silently-skipped assertion is a green that proves nothing. A fourth check was then added because *"answering NO writes nothing"* is **also true of a button that does nothing at all** (bug class 16) — the YES path is now proven to still pay.
- **738** · a priced document with no price asks before it goes out · First of the four form-validation items. Both `status:'sent'` paths — the editor's **Email to client** and the **Mark sent** toggle — had **no total guard**, so an estimate or contract reading **$0.00** went to a client with nothing said. **The design question that mattered was not "how do I block $0" but "what must I never block."** Measured: `id="estTotal"` appears in **every priced template** — `ESTIMATE_TEMPLATE_RAW`, `EST_TOTAL_ROW`, `GUTTER_BODY`, `CONTRACT_BODY`, `ROOF_/SIDING_/GUTTER_AGREEMENT_BODY`, `INVOICE_BODY`, `ANDERSEN_BODY` — and **NOT in `REPORT_TEMPLATE`**, the inspection report. So `priceOkToSend()` keys on the document's own shape rather than on a type list: `readEstimateTotal()` returns **`null` when there is no `#estTotal` node at all** (an inspection report — waved straight through), **`0`** only when a genuinely priced document totals zero, and a number otherwise. **There is no document-type whitelist to keep in step**, which is the point — `STAGES`/`IC_SKIP`/`PIPE_SKIP` are this file's cautionary tale about lists that must grow together. **It ASKS rather than refuses**, deliberately: a no-charge warranty estimate is a real thing, and a guard that blocks legitimate work is worse than the bug it fixes. **Un-marking is never questioned** — that direction is a correction, not a claim. `confirm()` 81 → 82, asserted (exactly one added, none removed). `gate_738.mjs`: **17 green on 738, 8 red on the v737 control**, driving four real documents through the shipped editor — a $0 estimate, a $17,025 estimate, an inspection report with no total node, and an already-sent doc. **The assertion that earns the build is the wave-through**: the inspection report reads `readEstimateTotal() === null`, is **never questioned**, and is marked sent exactly as before — proven, not assumed. The control reports the defect precisely: on v737 the $0 estimate is marked sent with `asked: []` and `sent writes = 1` **while the confirm stub is answering NO**. A YES-path check is included because "answering NO wrote nothing" is also true of a dead button (bug class 16). Wording was fixed after the first green run — the message read *"This Estimate — Bob DeBuilder has no total"*; it now quotes the title.
- **739** · phone numbers get one shape, and the field-validation convention is born · Second of the four. **Measured before building: there is no phone validation anywhere** — `replace(/\D/g` **0**, 10-digit checks **0**, no formatter, `type="tel"` ×8 setting only the mobile keypad. Every writer does `.value.trim()`, so the same number is stored a different way each time. **There was also no invalid-field convention at all** — `.invalid` 0, `.field-error` 0, `aria-invalid` 0, a shake keyframe 0 — so this build creates it ONCE (`<style id="cr-valid-styles">`, `.cr-bad`, `@keyframes crShake`) and items three and four reuse it rather than each inventing a second. **ONE DELEGATED LISTENER, not eight edits.** The tel inputs live in six different modules (`#upPhone`, `#pfPhone`, `#ldInsAdjPhone`, `.tmPhone`, two `[data-f="phone"]`, `homeowner_phone`, `renter_phone`, `#qiNpPhone`) and several are written by `innerHTML`, so per-module wiring would be eight edits the next new field would not inherit. **`blur` does not bubble — `capture:true` is what makes this work**, and the gate proves it by injecting a `type="tel"` input the app has never seen and blurring it. Events inside `#reportFrame` belong to another document and never reach the listener, which is correct: those are printed forms, not app fields (asserted, `contentDocument !== document`). **The rule that matters most: input the formatter does not understand is FLAGGED and NEVER REWRITTEN.** `937-555-0101 x123` and `+44 20 7946 0958` keep their text exactly and get the red border — a formatter that silently eats an extension is worse than no formatter. Seven input shapes normalise to `(937) 555-0101` including `+1` and a bare leading `1`; **blank stays valid**, because most of these fields are genuinely optional and refusing a blank would block real work. `gate_739.mjs`: **24 green on 739, 23 red on the v738 control.** It also asserts **`.cr-bad` actually paints** (`rgb(200,32,46)` border + a real box-shadow) rather than being an inert class, and that `crValid.shake` applies a real `crShake` animation and cleans up after itself. ⚠️ **The control CRASHED on the first run** rather than reporting red — `window.crValid` does not exist on v738, so every field read threw. Guarded: *a gate that throws on its negative control has not been seen to fail, it has been seen to break.* Same fault as gate_733's first cut, which is why it was recognised immediately.

- **740** · email addresses are checked, and the one a bid is sent to is fenced · Third of the four. **Measured before building: THIRTEEN email fields, none of them checked.** Nine `type="email"` and four more named `*email` but typed `text` — `cr-claims` `adjuster_email`, `cr-sol`, `cr-ci`, and `cr-crew`'s `contact_email`, whose placeholder literally reads *"never guess this one"*. ⚠️ **`type="email"` only constrains a NATIVE form submit, and every one of these saves through a JS handler**, so the attribute was doing nothing but setting a keyboard. **And the browser's own check is looser than people assume: `galen@habitat` passes `checkValidity()`** — no dot required — which the gate asserts, because it is the reason a handler-side check is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces. **The regex already existed** — `/^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$/` guards four money paths (draws, commissions, pay-draw, invite). Those four working call sites were **deliberately not rewritten** (churn with real regression risk on money, no user-visible gain); the same pattern was given one name, `crValid.email`, so new code stops re-deciding what an address looks like. The **one weak site** was upgraded: `cr-bulk`'s Reassign tested `/@/`, so `nick@` sailed through — and `assigned` is matched against that exact string by the sales RLS policy, so a half-typed address hands the selected clients to nobody and reports success. **The listener GREW A BRANCH; it did not gain a twin.** 739's delegated `blur` handler now dispatches tel vs email, so the count of capturing blur listeners is unchanged at 2 (the other is `cr-gmap`'s own autocomplete). ⚠️ **The self-check for that caught my own comment** — the first run failed 2→3 because the new comment quoted the call it was describing. The comment was reworded; the assertion was not weakened. Same class as 732 and 737. **THE FENCE, and why this one refuses instead of warning.** `CLAUDE.md`: *never write an unverified email address into `community_partners` — a bid sent to a guessed address is a lost bid.* That is not abstract — measured in the main block, when a community bid is emailed the recipient **defaults to the partner's `contact_email`** (`select('name,contact_email')` → `toDflt`). So a typo stored there is the address a bid goes to. `save()` is **exported** on `window.CardinalCommunityPartners`, so the refusal lives in `save()` (the fence) and the explanation in the form (the UI) — this module's own **635** doctrine, applied again. It fires **only when the key is present AND non-empty**, so **712 holds**: a rep saving a notes change still writes and still never touches the stored contacts, and a blank `contact_email` is still legal (five live partners have none). Both are asserted. **Bad input is flagged, never rewritten** — `email()` trims and does nothing else; case is left alone because case can be significant in a local part. `gate_740.mjs`: **49 green on 740, 37 red on the v739 control**, including the control writing the malformed address to the database. Regression sweep 721–739 all green.
- **741** · required fields say so, and a refused save moves the eye to the field · Last of the four. **Two measurements changed the design before a line was written.** ⚠️ **THE APP'S OWN "Name is required." MESSAGE WAS DEAD CODE.** `#cpForm` carries `<input name="name" required>` and submits natively, so the **browser blocked first** — probed in Chromium, `submitFired = FALSE`, `#cpErr` never rendered. Same shape on `#cpropForm`. Wiring a shake into a handler that never runs would have shipped **BUG_CLASSES 16** all over again, so both forms got `novalidate` and the app took its own failure back. **The gate asserts BOTH halves**: the handler now runs, *and* it still refuses (0 writes) — if the first passed and the second failed, the build would have opened a hole. A filled-in name still saves, asserted, so it is not a dead form. ⚠️ **THE ASTERISK ALREADY EXISTED FIVE WAYS**: `<span class="req">*</span>` (cr-nbid/cr-sol/cr-ci, in **three different colours** — red, `#fcd34d` amber, `#f08a90` pink), a literal `" *"` in label text (cr-nachi ×3, `pfName`), `placeholder="Name *"` (`qiNpName`), and `placeholder="…(required)"` (cr-estimates). And **six fields carrying `required` had no mark at all** — cr-pricing sku/name/rate, cr-claims amount, cr-cpartners name, cr-cprop address. Those six were marked. ⚠️ **A DERIVED CSS RULE WAS THE FIRST DESIGN AND IT IS WRONG.** `label:has(+ input[required])::after` is right for `<label>SKU</label><input required>` — but the other structure is `<label>Name<input required></label>`, where `::after` renders **after the input**, dropping a stray asterisk below the box. Two structures, so the mark is placed in the label text, **extending the convention the app already has** instead of inventing a mechanism beside it. `.cr-req`, not `.req`, because `req` is already taken four times over — including cr-shim's section badge reading "Required" / "4 min · 8 max". cr-sol's amber and cr-ci's pink are **left alone**: module palettes are a theming decision, not a validation one. `crValid.require(el, msg)` marks, shakes, focuses and returns `false`, so a guard reads as one line; it is null-safe because several of these run where the field may not be rendered. **Six guards wired**: cr-cpartners, cr-cprop, cr-estimates, cr-cadj, `pfName`, `qiNpName`. ⚠️ **Two harness faults, both mine, both caught by the gate.** The anchor for cr-cprop's guard assumed two lines where the file has one (**aborted before any write** — `patch_lib`'s assert did its job). And the asterisk count read `document.documentElement.outerHTML`, which contains **both a script's string literal and the element rendered from it** when a form is open — it reported 7 for 6. **The live DOM is not the source file.** Now reads the file. `gate_741.mjs`: **26 green on 741, 18 red on the v740 control**, the control showing `Add Property: the handler runs (false)` — the dead-message bug, confirmed on the previous build. Regression sweep 721–740 all green, including explicit re-assertions that 739's phone normalisation and 740's email flag still work.
- **742** · three readers treated a text column as an object · **Found while chasing something else, and measured against PRODUCTION rather than inferred.** `projects.checklist` is a **`text`** column (`information_schema.columns.data_type = text`, queried against the live database), so supabase-js hands back a **string**. Every writer does `pr.checklist = JSON.stringify(...)` and every reader goes through `parseCkAll(pr)` — **43 sites**. Four sites did not, and `.lead` on a string is `undefined`. **(1) The client CSV.** `var lead = (p.checklist && p.checklist.lead) || {}` made `lead` `{}` on every row, always, so **four of the eight exported columns were wrong for every client**: `claim_type` fell through to a hardcoded `'retail'`, and phone / email / assigned exported blank. Production is 34 clients — 16 community, 13 retail, 2 insurance, 2 none, 1 unknown — so **21 of 34 rows (62%) were mislabelled, including all 16 community jobs**, which are precisely the ones where a partner is billed and NOT the homeowner. 30 of 34 have an `assigned` value and every one exported blank. **Every CSV this app has ever produced was wrong in those columns.** **(2) and (3) Two health checks that could never fail.** `check_3_invalidClaimType` and `check_7_insTypeNoClaim` both filter on `p.checklist && p.checklist.lead && …`, always `undefined`, so both filters were always empty and both reported **"None found" regardless of the data** — BUG_CLASSES 15, an assertion incapable of failing. They happen to be telling the truth today (0 genuinely invalid types — `unknown` IS in the `VALID` map — and both insurance clients do carry claim numbers), which is exactly what makes them dangerous: **right by luck, not by looking.** ⚠️ **The scope was bounded by measurement, and MOST of the hits are prose.** A sweep for `.checklist.<word>` returns **18** hits; **13 are module banner comments** describing `checklist.meas` / `checklist.lead…` — the comment-pollution trap this file documents — leaving **4 distinct code sites (6 regex hits**, because `p.checklist && p.checklist.lead && p.checklist.lead.claim_type` matches an alternating pattern twice on one line; my first assertion said 5 and my own gate caught the arithmetic). ⚠️ **The neighbouring columns are jsonb and were deliberately NOT touched.** `contracts.contract`, `punch_items.comments`/`photos`, `estimates.photos` and `insurance_supplements.items` are all `jsonb`, so object access there is CORRECT — `check_2`'s `c.contract.signature` is not a bug, and the gate asserts it was left alone. Over-applying this fix would have broken a working check. `meas_docs.data` and `project_photos.data` are text but only ever handled as opaque strings. **No new mechanism.** The "read the lead block" idiom already exists in **four** named variants (`cdCrmOf`, `claimTypeOf`, `crmOf`, a module-local `lead`), so a fifth global would have been a mechanism beside an existing one; these use the existing inline idiom plus `window.projClaimType(p)`, the canonical resolver (20 window-qualified callers) which answers `'unknown'` instead of guessing `'retail'`. Phones and emails are joined with `'; '` exactly as `assigned` already was in the same object literal — the column is empty today so there is no behaviour to preserve, and dropping a client's second number would be a new bug. ⚠️ **`gate_742.mjs`'s SEED is the load-bearing part**: `checklist` is seeded as a JSON **string** because that is the production shape. Seed it as an object and the gate goes green on the broken code. **25 green on 742, 11 red on the v741 control**, the control printing `Betty Mann — Habitat,10 Elm St,Approved,retail,,,,` — the defect in one line. Regression sweep 721–741 all green.
- **743** · a phone number finds its client, whatever shape it was typed in · **Seven** search boxes carry a client phone — `renderHome`, `ljMatches`, `cdMatch`, `renderInsuranceClientsList` (main) and `cr-search-script` / `cr-ic-script` / `cr-ch2-script` — and all seven did a RAW substring match on `pr.phone`. (Three more — `cr-estimates`, `cr-eaf`, `cr-bpa` — search name+address only and were left alone.) **Two problems, one pre-existing and one mine, and the pre-existing one is bigger.** **(1) NOT ONE of the seven looked inside `checklist.lead.phones`.** Queried against production: 34 clients, **16 of whom keep a phone ONLY in the lead block** — so searching for those people by number has never worked, in any box, ever. **(2) My own drift from 739**: the blur handler rewrites a `type="tel"` field to `(937) 555-0101` and the save reads `.value` after blur, so numbers stored from now on carry that shape. Production today is 7 bare-10-digit / 3 dashed / 1 other / **0 pretty**, so nothing was broken yet — this lands before the data drifts rather than after. **THE DESIGN, and why it is 7 edits and not 14.** The obvious fix normalises the QUERY and compares against a digits-only haystack — but that needs both the haystack AND the comparison changed at each site, and the comparison lines are **not unique** (`return hay.indexOf(q) !== -1;` ×3, `if(hay.indexOf(q) === -1) return false;` ×3), so half would need block slicing. Instead the **haystack carries every common rendering** (digits, dashes, dots, spaces, brackets) and the existing `indexOf` matches whatever is typed — **the comparison logic is not touched at all**, which makes the change strictly ADDITIVE. Digit extraction delegates to `window.crValid.phone` (739), including its leading-1 rule, rather than re-deciding what a phone is. **The gate's headline assertion is NOT "more things match" — it is that NOTHING STOPPED matching.** `gate_743.mjs` fuzzes **161 query strings × 6 clients** (substrings of names, addresses, emails, POs and phones in every punctuation) against the OLD and NEW haystacks and fails on a single lost match: **0 lost, 14 gained**. A "we added matches" gate would pass even if the change broke searching by name. ⚠️ **The gate caught a real bug in my helper.** `phoneForms` early-returned on `d === raw`, a guard meant only to skip a duplicate — so a number STORED as bare digits never gained its punctuated forms and was findable only as itself. **4 red**, fixed, re-run green. ⚠️ **And the negative control CRASHED rather than reporting red** (`window.phoneHay is not a function`) — the same failure gate_739 hit. A gate that throws on its control has not been *seen to fail*; it has been seen to break. Guarded, then **21 red on the v742 control**. Regression sweep 721–742 all green.
- **744** · a date-only column stops displaying one day early · **Theo asked for currency and date FORMATTING. The audit found a correctness bug underneath it, and his premise was right about where.** **THE DAY SHIFT.** 30 columns in this database are Postgres **`date`** (`information_schema`), and PostgREST returns them as a bare string — verified against production: `date_of_loss` → `"2025-07-23"`, `valid_through` → `"2026-08-23"`, `scheduled_at` → `"2026-08-14"`. `new Date('2026-08-15')` parses as **UTC midnight**, which is 8pm on Aug 14 in Dayton. **Proven in Chromium**, not reasoned about: the same `toLocaleDateString` call gives **"Aug 14, 2026"** from the bare string and **"Aug 15, 2026"** from `+'T00:00:00'`. So a date-only column displayed **A DAY EARLY** — including `date_of_loss`, which goes on carrier correspondence, and `valid_through`, so an estimate expired a day before it said. **Only 3 of 15 formatters guarded it** (`cr-cc` fmtDay, `cr-show` fmtDate, and the main block's `commDate`, which is why the commissions and collections dates were already right). The other twelve are fixed. **AND THE RAW DATES WERE REAL — they are in Crews.** Three sites rendered a date column with no formatter at all: `'expires ' + row.expires_on` ×2 in the compliance vault, `esc(p.paid_on)` in the payments table, and `woVal(opts.scheduled_on)` on the **printed crew work order**. ⚠️ `cr-crew` has **zero** `toLocaleDateString` in 30,577 chars, yet its `daysLeft()` already parsed correctly with `iso + `'T00:00:00'` — so the “expires in N days” **arithmetic was right all along while the date printed beside it was raw**. `daysLeft` is untouched and asserted. **THE FIX IS A DROP-IN, and that is the load-bearing property.** `crDate(v)` returns exactly what `new Date(v)` returns for every input EXCEPT a bare `YYYY-MM-DD`, which it builds at LOCAL midnight. It never returns null, so every existing `isNaN(d)` / `isNaN(d.getTime())` / `d ? … : '—'` guard behaves identically. ⚠️ **The gate caught a real deviation in my first version**: it did `String(v)` before testing, so a NUMBER of epoch ms, `null` and a boolean all changed meaning — `String(0)` is `"0"` and `new Date("0")` is **the year 2000**, not the epoch. **3 red.** Now only a `typeof v === 'string'` is inspected; everything else goes straight to the native constructor. ⚠️ **FENCE: 35 `<input type="date">` values MUST stay `YYYY-MM-DD`** — that is what the HTML date picker binds. Nothing here touches an input value and the count is asserted unchanged. **`gate_744.mjs` runs in THREE timezones on purpose.** A day-shift bug is **invisible in UTC**, so a gate that only ran there would go green on the broken code. New York and Los Angeles are behind UTC (the bug bites); **Tokyo is ahead and was never affected**, which proves the fix is not merely “add a day”. It also fuzzes the drop-in equivalence over timestamps, junk, `Date` objects, numbers, `null` and booleans, and checks both DST boundary dates. **26 green on 744, 15 red on the v743 control** — the control printing `fmtDay('2026-08-15')` as **Aug 14** in New York and Los Angeles and **Aug 15** in Tokyo. Regression sweep 721–743 all green.
- **745** · money that names a specific amount stops rounding · Second half of Theo's item 7. **The audit killed two thirds of what I was going to build.** There are 20 money formatters producing four different answers for 34050, but they are not all wrong: `cr-adj`'s and `cr-hub`'s `money(n)` return `"34,050"` with **no dollar sign** — and **every one of their 9 call sites writes `'$' + money(...)`**. "Fixing" those would have printed **$$34,050** at nine places. **A false positive I caught before shipping, and reported to Theo as one.** Only `cr-abc`'s `usd()` was genuinely wrong (`toFixed(2)`, no thousands separator → `$34050.00`). **THE REAL DEFECT WAS `fmtMoney`, the dominant formatter with 33 call sites**: `if(!n) return '--'` and `Math.round(n)`. Rounding is *right* on a dashboard tile and wrong the moment a number names a specific amount — and it was on **the invoice**. `[INV_TOTAL]` / `[INV_PAID]` / `[INV_DUE]` all went through it, so **a client invoice for $1,702.50 printed $1,703, and an unpaid invoice printed `--` in the Paid box**. Measured end-to-end: the v744 control generates an invoice containing `["$1,703","$1,703"]` — rounded, and the Paid line **missing entirely** because `--` is not money. On 745 the same invoice reads `["$1,702.50","$0.00","$1,702.50"]`. **NO NEW MECHANISM — and the prime doctrine bit me for missing half of it.** `cr-crew-script` has had `money(n, cents)` since **556**, so `fmtMoney` grew the same second argument. But cr-crew's version also puts **the sign OUTSIDE the symbol** (`sign + '$' + Math.abs(v)`), with a comment saying why, and my first version copied the cents flag *without* it — `fmtMoney(-500, true)` returned **`$-500.00`**. **gate_745 went red on exactly that.** Copy the whole solution, not the half you were looking at. **The default is byte-for-byte unchanged**, so the other 24 callers — tiles, reports, KPIs — render identically; the gate **fuzzes the default against the OLD implementation over 30 values** and fails on any divergence, because without that this build could have quietly restyled 24 screens. Nine sites opt in: the three invoice tokens, the two `auditLog('money', …)` entries, and the four messages that name a figure back to whoever just entered it. ⚠️ **Two harness faults, both mine.** The gate's money extractor had `--` in its alternation, and `INVOICE_TEMPLATE` is ~148 KB of mostly CSS — **every `--ink` / `--line` custom property matched**, so it scored twelve `--` and zero amounts and read as a total failure on a build that was working. And the invoice button only renders once the worksheet panel has painted, so the gate now drives `createInvoiceFor()` — the shipped function the button calls — directly. ⚠️ **`gate_734` went red in the sweep and the GATE was what was stale, not the app.** It computed its expectation as `fmtMoney(1702.5)` while the call site now asks for cents; the toast legitimately changed from `$1,703` to `$1,702.50`. Updated to compute in the same mode as the call site. Roughly half of all reds on this project are the test's fault and this was one. **26 green on 745, 13 red on the v744 control.** Regression sweep 721–744 all green.
- **746** · Company Documents: Download stops swallowing the app · Theo: *"in company documents it says view and download but download doesn't download and you can't get back to the crm."* **Both halves reproduced, and the second is one missing attribute.** **(1) TWO OF THE FIVE LISTED DOCUMENTS DO NOT EXIST.** Checked against production with `curl`, not assumed: `Cardinal_Roofing_Contract.pdf` **200**, `Cardinal_Siding_Contract.pdf` **200**, `Cardinal_Window_Contract.pdf` **404**, `Cardinal_Gutter_Contract.pdf` **200**, `Cardinal_Gutter_Contract_Fillable.pdf` **404**. `COMPANY_DOCS` lists five; `docs/` holds three. On two of five rows BOTH buttons led to a 404 — *"download doesn't download"*, exactly. **This was a standing OPEN_ITEMS entry and Theo has now hit it.** **(2) AND THAT IS WHY YOU CANNOT GET BACK.** The two links were not the same: View carried `target="_blank" rel="noopener"`; **Download carried no target at all**. The `download` attribute is honoured on desktop but **not reliably for a PDF on iOS Safari** — the file opens instead — and with no target that navigation **replaces the app in place**. Theo works from an iPad, and **an installed PWA has no browser back button**, so the CRM is gone until the app is force-closed. One attribute, and the way out with it. **The 404 half is a HEAD probe, deliberately not a `missing:true` flag** — a flag has to be remembered, whereas the probe means the row starts working by itself the moment the PDF is uploaded, with no code change. ⚠️ **It downgrades a row on a definite 404 and NOTHING ELSE.** A network error, an offline PWA or a slow reply leaves the buttons exactly as they are, because **refusing to offer a document that IS there would be a worse bug than the one being fixed** — `gate_746.mjs` proves it by killing the HEAD request for `Cardinal_Gutter_Contract.pdf` at the network layer and asserting that row keeps both buttons. **15 green on 746, 9 red on the v745 control**, the control showing all five Download links with `target: ""` and all five rows advertising as available including the two that 404. Regression sweep 721–745 all green. **Print styles were audited in the same turn and are NOT part of this build** — see the print section in `FEATURES.md`. Short version: the app already hides its chrome (**0 of 508** buttons/inputs/nav paint under print media, measured), so that third of the ask is done; but the document templates carry **0** `page-break-*` rules in 155 KB, the logo appears on page 1 only, and the `PROPERTY PHOTO` placeholder prints as a **459,580 px² solid grey block** when no photo is attached. Those want Theo's eye on a legal document before anything moves.
- **747** · printed documents: no photo on contracts, a header on every page, breaks in the right places · Theo's three answers to the 746 print audit: *"Take out property photos on contracts"*, running header **"Slim"**, page breaks *"whatever looks more professional"*. **ONE SEAM, NINE DOCUMENT TYPES.** Every priced document is `buildEstimate(title, body, terms)` substituting into a skeleton — so the three agreements, the Service Contract, the Invoice and the estimates are all reached at once. ⚠️ **There are TWO skeletons, not one**: `ESTIMATE_BASE_RAW` (everything via `buildEstimate`) and the older `ESTIMATE_TEMPLATE_RAW` (the ROOF estimate, `EST_TYPES.roof`). They share the same CSS tail, so a file-wide anchor matches twice — **the first run aborted on exactly that, before any write**. Both get the treatment. ⚠️ **THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTED AND WAS UNUSED**: both skeletons already defined `.avoid-break{break-inside:avoid}` and `.page-break{break-before:page}` and applied them to the markup **zero times**. ⚠️ **`position:fixed` IS THE ONLY RUNNING-HEADER MECHANISM THAT WORKS, and it was measured, not assumed.** Counting the header's colour band in each page's own content stream: `position:fixed` = **5 of 5 pages**, `<thead>` = 5 of 5. **`@page` margin boxes are not implemented in Chrome or Safari**, which is why there is deliberately **no "page N of M"** — `counter(page)` only resolves inside a margin box. The browser's own print footer supplies page numbers. ⚠️ A `position:fixed` header sits in the page CONTENT box, so `body{padding-top}` is required or page 2 onward prints text underneath it. **The photo is stripped in `buildEstimate`, not deleted from the skeleton** — gated on the heading text, so an AGREEMENT/CONTRACT drops it and an ESTIMATE keeps it. `isContractTitle`/`isEstimateTitle`/`docKind` are deliberately NOT reused: they test a SAVED document's title, not a template heading, and all three are declared AFTER `buildEstimate`, which runs at parse time. Estimates additionally gained the `.cover-photo:not(:has(img))` print rule `REPORT_TEMPLATE` has had all along. ⚠️ **The gate's first split-detector was measuring the wrong thing and went 2 red against a correct build.** It modelled pagination as `scrollHeight/1056` and flagged rows straddling a boundary — but `break-inside:avoid` changes NOTHING in continuous layout; it only acts when the engine paginates, and it moves the row. Chromium exposes no per-element page assignment, so the honest assertions are **computed style under print media** (the rules apply) plus **the real PDF** (the header band on every page). **26 green on 747, 19 red on the v746 control** — the control measuring the empty property photo at **459,580 px²** and the header on **0 of 5 pages**, the two figures quoted to Theo in the audit. Rendered and eyeballed: the Customer Information table that used to split across pages 1→2 now fits entirely on page 1, and "Warranty System" is no longer stranded at the foot of page 2. Regression sweep 721–746 all green.

- **748** · the three Construction Agreements get real tick boxes · Theo: *"when doing a new contract… it says to circle but only does text edits and looks nothing like the actual contract with check boxes."* **He was right, and THE PRIME DOCTRINE PAID AGAIN — clickable checkboxes already existed and already shipped.** `.cbx{cursor:pointer;font-size:13pt;user-select:none;}` was already in `ESTIMATE_BASE_RAW`, the very skeleton all three Agreements are built from; `wireCheckboxes(doc)` already existed and was **already called from `openEditor`'s onload**, once, for every document it opens; and two documents were already using it in production — GUTTER_BODY's size boxes (`data-val`) and ANDERSEN_BODY's series boxes (`data-group`). The Agreements were simply the only priced documents that never got pointed at it. **So this build adds ZERO javascript and ZERO css** — asserted three ways — and converts markup only: **25 `[circle one]` / `[circle all that apply]` prompts → 76 tick boxes** (roof 23, siding 21, gutter 32). Grouped boxes (`data-group`) behave as radios; ungrouped ones are the "all that apply" rows (roof flashing, gutter miters). Lettering (A. / B. / C.) is preserved exactly so the screen and the paper master read the same. **The gutter agreement's "No gutter protection on this job" had been drawn as a `&#9633;` WHITE SQUARE with no class since it shipped — it looked like a checkbox and had never been clickable** (BUG_CLASSES 16, again); it now joins the ShurFlo group, so ticking it clears A/B/C. ⚠️ **`.opts` spans were left alone on purpose** — decking/layers/pitch are not choice prompts, they are the `collapse()` auto-fill from the roof inspection, and its regex `[^<]*(?:<(?!/span>)[^<]*)*` stops at the first `</span>`, so a box inside one would truncate the match and break the fill. `gate_748.mjs`: **77 green on 748, 56 red on the v747 control.** It drives the **real `#reportFrame` with the app's own `lockTemplate` / `wireCheckboxes` / `serializeFrame`** — no re-implementation — and the assertion that earned the browser is that **every new box sits inside a `contenteditable` cell** (`table.meta td:not(.k)` is in `EDITABLE_SELECTOR`), so a caret lives where the click lands; it asserts the cell IS editable, then clicks it anyway, and also does one **hit-tested real mouse click** through the visible editor. It further proves the ticks **survive `serializeFrame()`**, that the save strips `data-cbx` so a reopened contract re-wires, and that re-wiring twice does not double-bind. Printed: the glyph measures 16×19 px (not a zero-width tofu), a ticked box prints ticked, and the on-screen "tap a box" hint does not print. ⚠️ **The gate went 1 red against a correct build first**: it asserted ANDERSEN_TEMPLATE had 5 boxes, counted from source literals — but `cbxColor()` generates one per colour, so the built document has **23, on 747 and 748 alike**. Measured on the control, not counted in the source (BUG_CLASSES 15). ⚠️ And its **negative control CRASHED rather than going red** — new class 37.

- **749** · the roofing agreement gets the numbered house diagram · Theo: *"Can you do the house diagram with numbers"* — the second half of the 748 complaint. ⚠️ **IT IS NOT DRAWN. It is the master's own illustration, recovered from the PDF.** His words at 748 were that the on-screen contract "looks nothing like the actual contract"; answering that with a hand-drawn SVG would have repeated the same mistake in a new medium. `docs/Cardinal_Roofing_Contract.pdf` page 1 carries the cutaway as an embedded PNG (**xref 30, 1172×840, placed at 218×156 pt**); extracted with PyMuPDF, greyscaled, resized to 760 px, re-encoded JPEG q84 → **96,877 bytes / 129,195 as a data URI**. The eleven callouts map 1:1 onto the numbered spec rows it now sits above (1 decking · 2 deck protection · 3 drip edge · 4 ice & water ×3 · 5 valley metal · 6 starter · 7 shingles · 8 flashing · 9 extrusions · 10 ventilation · 11 ridge cap). 12 and 13 are counts, not places, so the master gives them no callout either. **Sizing was a measured decision, not a default**: the cost is *per saved document*, because `serializeFrame()` stores each contract's whole HTML — so the established precedent was measured first (**the Cardinal logo is ALREADY a 139,982-char data URI in every document `buildEstimate` makes**) and 749 was deliberately kept under it; 900 px (152 KB) and 1040 px (186 KB) were rejected on that basis. A saved agreement measures **281 KB**. ⚠️ **ROOFING ONLY, AND THAT IS MEASURED**: the siding and gutter masters were opened too and carry only the Cardinal logo and the BBB badge — there is no diagram to port. ⚠️ **The figure must not look like a photo slot**: `wireCoverPhoto()` claims `.cover-photo` and `wirePhotoFrames()` claims `.fig .frame`, both injecting a file input; all four doc-side `img` selectors were swept and are scoped, and `.roofdiag` is outside `EDITABLE_SELECTOR` too, so it cannot be typed over. `gate_749.mjs`: **37 green on 749, 23 red on the v748 control.** Its load-bearing assertion is `naturalWidth`/`naturalHeight` read from Chromium — a truncated or mangled data URI still yields an `<img>` element and still passes every structural check, so only the decoded dimensions prove the bytes survived the template literal. Prints at 346 px / **211 dpi**, capped at 3.6 in, `break-inside:avoid`. ⚠️ **Two self-inflicted faults, both recorded**: a CSS comment quoting a word in backticks **inside a template literal** would have closed `ESTIMATE_BASE_RAW` mid-stylesheet — caught by an assertion, then *reintroduced by the correction, which quoted it again* (new class 38); and the gate's first version matched `/roofdiag/` against the built documents, which all share one skeleton and therefore all contain the CSS rule, reporting a diagram in siding and gutters that does not exist, plus it grabbed `querySelector('table.meta')` — the FIRST such table is Customer Information, which sits **above** the figure. Three reds against a correct build, all gate faults.

- **750** · colour dropdowns on the roofing agreement · Theo: *"Can you make drop downs for oc colors and drip edge colors?"* **TWO LISTS FROM COMPLETELY DIFFERENT PLACES, and the audit is the build.** ⚠️ **OC shingle colours are real data and were already loaded**: `cr-occ-script` queries `oc_colors` with `.eq('hidden',false).order('sort_order')` and caches into a module-local `COLORS`. So this opened **no second pipeline** — `window.CardinalColors` gained a `list()` accessor (it exported only open/close/reload) and the document wiring calls it; **`from('oc_colors')` is still 1 file-wide, asserted**. `load()` was read first and touches `VIEW` nowhere, so it is safe with no hub mounted — and going through it means the dropdown **inherits the hidden filter and the sort order for free**, so Shasta White (the one hidden colour) stays out by construction rather than by a second rule, and discontinued colours keep their badged spot as `Storm Cloud (discontinued)`. Both are Theo's settled decisions, now enforced by reuse. ⚠️ **Drip edge / gutter apron colours existed NOWHERE** — no table, no constant; all 45 "drip edge" hits are Resource Library prose about RCO code. **I refused to invent a list silently onto a signed contract and asked**; Theo chose the standard aluminium stock range, so `TRIM_COLORS` is a **new hardcoded list, labelled as a starting list**, with `Other` on the end so a rep is never blocked. ⚠️ **THE HARD PART IS PERSISTENCE, NOT THE MARKUP.** A `<select>`'s value is a **PROPERTY**; `serializeFrame()` saves via `cloneNode(true)`, which copies **attributes only**. The obvious version looks perfect, passes every structural assertion, and **loses the colour the moment the contract is saved** with nothing in the DOM to show it ever held one. The `change` handler therefore writes the **`selected` ATTRIBUTE** and strips it from the others — the same shape as 748's checkboxes, whose state lives in `textContent`. Saved options are **deliberately frozen** into the document: an old contract shows the colours it was written with, not today's catalogue. `serializeFrame` strips `data-crsel-wired` exactly as it strips `data-cbx`. `gate_750.mjs` does the **full round trip through the app's own functions** — populate → change → `serializeFrame()` → reopen → re-read — **32 green on 750, 20 red on the v749 control**, seeded with a hidden row and a discontinued row so both rules are proven rather than asserted. ⚠️ **Scoped to the three fields Theo named**: item 5 **Valley metal colour is still free text on purpose** — same trim palette, but a fourth field he did not ask for, so it was raised with him instead of widened into. **Three assertions of mine were wrong before the app was** (`data-crsel-wired` is 4 sites not 3 because `removeAttribute` names it too; `.crsel{` is 2 rules not 1 because of the print override; and `[colour]` is 1 not 0 because of valley metal) — each was re-measured and the constant corrected, never the artifact.

- **751** · photos open as photos · Theo: *"when opening the photo gallery, when photo is touched it goes to client profile. Can you make it so it enlarges the photo … full screen and gives option to go to the profile or back arrow."* **THE PRIME DOCTRINE, THIRD TIME IN FOUR BUILDS.** A full-screen viewer already ships — `cr-ri-script` / `window.CardinalResourceImages.open(src, caption)`: fixed overlay, dark ground, caption, Escape, body scroll lock, **already called from six sites** including Punch & Repairs' zoom. Photo Activity's grid had simply never been pointed at it; its handler was four lines that went straight to `openProject(pid)`. **No viewer was written.** The grid now calls the existing one and the viewer gained an **optional** third argument, `opts {actionLabel, onAction}`, rendering a bar with **‹ Back** and **Open client ›**. ⚠️ **THE OVERLAY IS A SINGLETON** — `ensureZoom()` builds it once and every later `open()` reuses the node, so the action bar MUST be reset on every open or a gallery photo leaves an "Open client" button sitting on the next Resource Library figure, pointing at whichever client was last opened. `gate_751` opens WITH an action, closes, opens WITHOUT, and asserts the button is gone AND inert. ⚠️ **`zoom.onclick = close` means any click closes** — that is what makes tapping the photo dismiss it and six older callers depend on it, so the bar stops propagation and drives `close()` in its own order (reading `action` BEFORE close clears it). **No 14th scroll-lock writer**: the module was already one of the thirteen; `document.body.style.overflow` count is unchanged at 36, asserted. **Touch targets, as a down payment on the wider question Theo asked in the same message**: the viewer's close button measured **38×38 at 390px**, under his own 44px floor — now 44×44, with Back at 78×44 and Open client at 121×44, all measured as **rendered rects** in a touch-enabled 390px context. `gate_751.mjs`: **26 green on 751, 25 red on the v750 control.** ⚠️ **SIX of my own assertions were wrong before the app ever was** — `data-ri="go"` is 4 sites not 3; `action = null;` is 2 not 1 because the declaration contains it; `function close(){` appears **21 times** so `src.index()` found another module's; `width:44px;height:44px;` already existed **14 times** (44px is an existing convention here, not a new one); the viewer calls are **6 not 9** because `grep -c` counts LINES and three hits are `typeof` guards; and the "38px is gone" check tripped on **six unrelated 38px controls**. Every one was re-measured and the constant corrected, never the artifact.

- **752** · the 44px touch-target floor · Theo's item 10, scope **3** ("everything measured") picked by number after the seven-screen walk (`walk751.mjs` — 390px, touch context, **rendered rects**; home alone was **74 of 89 controls under 44px**). **ONE late `<style id="cr-touch44-styles">` block carries the ENTIRE pass** — no colours, no `!important`, and the census IS the block, so the partial-pass trap (13-of-14 reads as done) has nowhere to live. ⚠️ **The mechanism is `min-width`/`min-height`, and that choice is what made one block possible**: the offenders are sized by id-scoped rules a class selector cannot out-specify (`#calCard .calnav{width:32px}`, `#leadsView .ljbtn{width:38px}`), but min-* are **different properties** — they never compete with width/height in the cascade; used value = max(width, min-width). So a plain-class rule beats an id-scoped width while every module stylesheet stays byte-identical (asserted). Raised: header chrome (menu/＋/home/back/theme, 30–38 → 44) · all 16+ nav items (33 → 44) · the **60 Call/Text pills** on home cards (29 → 44) · calendar arrows (28 → 44) · the 15 `.ljbtn` card actions (36–38 → 44) · filter chips + the 87×20 sort control · the profile's **12px-tall** contact links (`a.hem`/`a.hph`/`#dbAddContact`/`#dbSwitchPrim`, now inline-flex 44) · edit pencil · Map/Satellite toggles · `.chipbtn` app-wide (covers Mark Paid / Mark repaid / Remove money actions, `.pay-btn`/`.pay-chip` too) · `.pp-add` (139×36, **not a chipbtn** — the first gate run caught the census assuming it was) · `select{min-height:44px}` app-wide. **Untouched on purpose**: printed documents (the `#reportFrame` iframe is a separate document app CSS cannot reach — the 15px contract tick boxes still print at 15px, asserted), photo tiles (155px, already over), and **`.pu-box`**. ⚠️ **`.pu-box` is the session's best prime-doctrine find in miniature**: it measured 22×22 and looked like an offender, but `cr-punch2-styles` already gives it a **44×44 `::after` hit box** — `getBoundingClientRect` cannot see pseudo-element hit areas, so **a rect-based touch audit under-reports any control using this pattern**. Do not "fix" it into a visible 44px square. `gate_752.mjs`: **32 green on 752, 27 red on the v751 control**; home under-44 count **74 → 1** (the one survivor is pu-box, correct by ::after). ⚠️ **The gate itself went red twice against a correct build, both instrument faults, both kept as comments**: `elementFromPoint` answers **null outside the viewport** (the punch strip sits below the fold — the first probe "missed" every tap including the box's own centre), and in the seeded harness the landing module paints over the home strip, so no elementFromPoint claim about the covered control is honest — the gate now asserts the computed `::after` box instead of the tap. Screenshots before/after at 390px (home/menu/list/profile): menu and list read better; **the profile hero is airier** (two 44px contact rows where four 12px links huddled) and the header's RETAIL pill row wraps below the search bar — both visible in the pair images handed to Theo, his eyes are that gate. Also: Playwright's `page.screenshot` hangs "waiting for fonts" under the mock — CDP `Page.captureScreenshot` has no such wait and is the workaround on record.


- **753** · the Menu and + menus open under their buttons · Theo: *"the burger menu is in left but opens right."* **Root cause measured, not read**: the navBtn click handler HAS positioned the menu against the button since forever — but `cr-menu-styles` pins `#navMenu{left:auto !important;right:10px !important}`, written when the Menu button lived at the right of the old masthead. cr-hd2 (416) moved the button to the left end of the bar, and an `!important` stylesheet rule beats any inline style, so the handler lost silently: probe showed inline `right:1021px` vs computed `right:10px`. Same class as the `#tab-overview` allow-list — the code runs, the stylesheet wins, and reading the code says it works. **The + menu carried the identical bug in its handler itself** ("The + button sits at the top-right" — not since 416): right-edge-aligned to a left-side button, it opened **80px off-screen at 768px** (measured x=[-80..110]). Both menus now drop from their button's left edge and clamp on-screen against their real rendered width after display. The pins are gone; every other `!important` in cr-menu-styles (width, scroll, max-height) survives, asserted. `gate_753.mjs`: 37 green at 390/768/1194/2560 incl. delegation sanity; **11 red on the v752 control**. ⚠️ Instrument note for the next screenshotter: a style override appended to `<head>` loses the `!important` tie to `cr-menu-styles` (later in document order) — the first "fixed" screenshot silently showed the bug. Append simulation overrides to `<body>`.

- **754** · the header remembers which CRM you're in · Theo: *"It's retail only: so when I'm in insurance or community if u touch anything in the header it takes me to retail."* Confirmed by a full tap-table audit (`audit_header.mjs`): from Truth or the hub, EVERY banner pill and burger item lands on a shared screen, `crmNow()` answers 'retail' there (it derives the CRM from which view is open), the header repaints steel, and the gold home then points at the retail dashboard. **The app already had the answer**: the sticky per-user portal (`CardinalPortal`, localStorage) that the landing cards, both CRM homes (portal_view_sync) and the banner switcher all keep updated — the header just never asked it. New resolver `crmHead()`: **open view > open client's own claim type > sticky portal** ('all' → retail). ⚠️ **Two attributes on purpose — the naive fix is a readability regression, measured before rejecting it**: making `crmNow()` sticky flips `body[data-crm=insurance]{background:var(--ct-bg)}` under retail-styled shared screens, and "All Leads & Jobs" (white ink) went near-invisible on the light insurance ground. So `body[data-crm]` (page grounds, PIPE_SKIP, module gates, theme-toggle float) is untouched, and **26 header-chrome selector occurrences** (.site token blocks ×5, #cr-hd2-bar rules, ribbon ×4+inks, #crBanner ×2, --bn* strip tokens ×3, brand title) migrated to **`body[data-crm-head]`**. Two location-header rules stayed on `data-crm` **deliberately**: the insurance dark-toggle hide (3240) and `body:not([data-crm=insurance]) .cr-ins-theme` (55222) — the theme controls follow the PAGE they theme, or a shared screen would show two theme buttons at once. Routing on crmHead: gold home, banner ROUTES.home, switcher highlight (banner + left rail + rail accent), and `openLeadForm`'s default claim type — whose own comment already said "follow the portal you're standing in" while reading the view. `gate_754.mjs`: 27 green incl. rendered-paint identity between CRM home and shared screen and the page-ground-unchanged proof; **17 red on the v753 control** — every red is a line of Theo's complaint.

- **755** · the banner speaks your CRM's language · The two CRM-shaped pills follow `data-crm-head`: **Insurance → Clients / Claims** (`showInsuranceClients`, `crOpenClaims` — the app-level entry, history-wrapped, not the bare module open), **Community → Partners / Bids** (each deep-links `CardinalCommunityHome.tab()` — the hub's own panes, Theo's 711 pick — not the partner-directory modal). Retail keeps Contacts/Leads byte-for-byte and the swap reverses on every CRM change. **Same two elements re-labelled** (`paintCrmPills` in cr-banner-script, driven from cbCrmSync's observer pass, every write guarded) — not new pills beside old ones, the 417 duplicate-entrance class. Slots are tagged `data-cr-slot` because `data-go` stops being a stable handle once swapped. **Rider**: `#leadsView`'s static subtitle said "Retail only" while `ljMatches` has no CRM facet at all — mixed-CRM seeds all listed under that label, measured. It now says "All CRMs"; a real CRM filter there is Theo's call, not smuggled in. `gate_755.mjs`: 17 green incl. tab-level deep-links and the retail round-trip; **9 red on the v754 control** — after the control's first run CRASHED instead of reporting (a bare `.click()` on a pill that doesn't exist on v754; BUG_CLASSES 37, fixed in the gate).

- **756** · the header follows you onto the tool screens, and Home means YOUR CRM · Theo, from the Insurance Claims screen: *"Can you make the header follow the claims page. Also the home icon on the top right takes you to retail home. Can you also have it follow the same crm language."* **Three defects, all measured before a line was written.** (1) **The header was covered on a PHONE only** — the five module mounts are `position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:200` inline from `styleMounts()`, the header is z-index 90, and the rules that push them below it (561/572) are scoped `body.cr-lnav-on` = desktop only. At 390px all five sat at `top=0 z=200` with the header's home button failing a hit test (`elementFromPoint` returned the mount's floating exit button); at 1194px they were already `top=187 z=60`. **BUG_CLASSES 41.** (2) **Home did not close the tool screen — at EITHER width.** `showCardinalTruth()` / `showInsuranceClients()` / `showResourceLibrary()` hand-roll a four-view teardown and never call `hideAllViews()`, whose list carries the mounts; `showHome()` and the Community hub always did, which is why only insurance showed it. A MutationObserver on the mount recorded **zero** style writes — never hidden, not hidden-then-reshown. ⚠️ The `defineProperty` version of that instrument traces NOTHING regardless, because Blink serves style properties through a V8 interceptor with no descriptor to hook. Build 679 had already written "never went through hideAllViews()" in a comment while fixing only the symptom. **BUG_CLASSES 42.** (3) **Two home controls were CRM-blind** — `crCloseAll()` (behind `#cr-pme-exit-btn`, the button Theo tapped) and `#cr-home-btn` both called `showHome()` unconditionally. **The fix**: one `CardinalHeader.goHome()` that every home control calls (the gold house's own 754 ladder becomes its first caller, not a second copy); the three hub navigations route through `hideAllViews()`; one ungated rule puts all five mounts below the header at every width **using the same values the desktop rule already sets, so the desktop cannot move by construction**; and `.cr-pme-exit` drops to `calc(var(--headh) + 10px)` so it no longer floats over the header it used to replace. `--headh` already includes the notch. `gate_756.mjs`: **86 green across five mounts x two widths** — including a HIT TEST rather than a rect (a rect-only check passes on the broken build, since the header is laid out correctly and merely painted over) — and **40 red on the v755 control**. Scroll verified after the box shrank 186px: clientH 658, scrollH 2415, bottom reachable. ⚠️ Three of this patch's own assertions were wrong before the artifact ever was: a blanket "no backtick" flagged the 417 comment being *relocated* (fixed to a self-computing delta), a bare `hideAllViews()` count read +6 because **this patch's own comments name the function six times** (the .pu-box census trap again — count call statements), and one assertion demanded a fallback be deleted that was deliberately kept.

- **757** · one Home button, not three · Theo, after 756 put the header back on the tool screens: *"Retire redundant ones."* Measured at 390px on the Claims page, three Home controls were on screen at once: `#cr-hd2-home` (the gold house in the header), `#cr-home-btn` (floating in `#navWrap`, one row below it) and `#cr-pme-exit-btn` (floating on the panel itself). The last two are gone. ⚠️ **`#cr-home-btn` had ALREADY been retired once, in CSS** — `cr-hd2-styles` has carried `#cr-home-btn{display:none}` since the 416/417 header rebuild, and its module then wrote `btn.style.display='inline-flex'` **inline** on every observer pass. An inline style outranks any non-important stylesheet declaration, so the button outlived its own retirement by ~340 builds. That is the styleMounts trap wearing a different hat, and the file's own rule settles it: **deletion at source beats out-specificity.** **Kept deliberately**: cr-pme's **Escape key**, which closes whichever tool screen is open and is duplicated nowhere — it is the reason that module was gutted rather than deleted; `crCloseAll()` (two other modules call it); and `cr-home-cleanup`'s `updateHomeBtn()`, which already guarded `if(!btn) return`. Both dedicated stylesheets deleted with their buttons (`cr-home-btn-styles`, `cr-pme-styles`), along with 756's own `.cr-pme-exit` positioning rule — written one build earlier for a button that no longer exists. **Side benefit worth recording: two `document.body` MutationObservers retired, one of them `subtree:true`**, plus four per-mount attribute observers; CLAUDE.md's census is corrected in place and both modules struck from its list. Net **-2930 characters** (-2920 bytes) — 6,582 characters of button machinery and stylesheet removed, about 3.6 KB of it given back as the comments explaining why. ⚠️ The first draft of this line said "net −6.6 KB", which was the REMOVED figure, not the net; measured before it shipped. `gate_757.mjs`: **76 green across two widths** — it asserts not just that the two ids are absent but that **exactly ONE control titled "Home" is visible** on four ordinary screens and all five tool screens, re-checked after a settle window because both buttons were observer-driven and a single snapshot would not have caught a re-mount; plus the gold home still hit-testable and still closing each tool screen, and Escape still working. **34 red on the v756 control.**

- **758** · the text that ran off the screen · Two of Theo's four reports, and **one root cause behind both** — see BUG_CLASSES 43. (a) *"the cards run past the screen"*: `.cr-ic-list` is a grid whose implicit `1fr` track cannot shrink below its content, because a grid item is `min-width:auto` and `.cr-ic-row .ad` is `white-space:nowrap`. **Measured at 390px: the track computed to 405.5px inside a 358px container and both cards ended at x=422** — 32px off-screen, CLIPPED rather than scrollable because `html,body` carry `overflow-x:hidden`. Both cards overflow because grid items share a track width, which is why the short-address card was cut too. Fixed with `minmax(0,1fr)` + `min-width:0`. (b) *"the second box text running over… moving the address below the name"*: `.cr-pb-job .nm`/`.ad` are `<span>`s, so **`text-overflow:ellipsis` was inert** and the two ran together with no separator. Both now `display:block` — exactly what Theo prescribed. ⚠️ **The insurance address was the SAME inline bug and I nearly shipped it half-fixed**: the grid change stopped the *card* stretching, so the gate went green while the *text* still overflowed by 32px — because the truncation assertion (`scrollWidth <= clientWidth+1`) is **0 <= 1 on an inline box, a vacuous pass**. Caught by looking at the screenshot after the gate was green. `.cr-ic-row .ad` is block now and the gate asserts `display` plus the element's own right edge. Readability: `.cr-pb-job .ad`'s ink measured **3.23:1** on the card (under the 4.5 floor) → `#8d959d` = **5.33:1**, an ink the module already uses. ⚠️ Scope held deliberately: that hex appears **13 times, all in cr-pb-styles, all `color:`**, but it measures **5.07:1 on white** and this module has light overrides — a blanket swap would have fixed dark and broken light, the project's most repeated defect. Only the one site with an existing light twin was touched; the other 12 are measured and reported to Theo.

- **759** · the gallery follows your CRM, and a punch out can call the client · Theo's other two reports. (a) Photo Activity had **no CRM axis at all** — measured standing in Insurance: 12 tiles, 5 retail / 4 insurance / 3 community. `project_photos` carries no type column, so the CRM comes from the joined project through `projClaimType()`. Opening Photos now preselects the CRM you were in (`CardinalHeader.crmHead()`, 754) and a chip row widens it back; **untyped jobs count as retail**, the same default `crmNow()`/`crmHead()` use, so the buckets sum to the whole. The subtitle states the filter ("Insurance only · 4 of 12") so nothing is hidden silently. Chips reuse the app's existing `.ljchips`/`.ljchip` — no new stylesheet, and they inherit 752's 44px floor. (b) ⚠️ **CORRECTION TO MY OWN READ: the Call button already existed and was already styled** — `.cr-pb-dtel` shares a rule with `.cr-pb-dadd`; my grep for `cr-pb-dtel{` missed it because the selector sits in a **comma list**. The file's own rule applies: when a count contradicts you, suspect the regex. The real gaps were no icon and `pr.phone` only. **Measured on production (34 projects): 11 rows keep the number ONLY in `checklist.lead.homeowner_phone`** — so the button was invisible for a third of the book. New `projPhone()` beside `projHomeowner()` (same shape, auto-global), fallback order copied from `phoneHay()` (743), normalised through `crValid.phone()` rather than a ninth regex; reachability 11/34 → 22/34. ⚠️ **Only the dossier is repointed at it — seven other hand-rolled `String(pr.phone||'')` sites remain and are a named follow-up**, not swept blind inside a call-button build. ⚠️ **Told Theo plainly: Kimberly Guy, the client in his screenshot, has no phone in ANY of the five locations, so her card still shows no Call button.** That is missing data, not a bug. `gate_759.mjs`: **30 green across all four reports, 23 red on the v757 control**; the gate itself was corrected twice — a vacuous inline-box assertion (above) and a backtick inside its own template literal (BUG_CLASSES 38, in the gate this time).

The gate asserts `display` plus the element's own right edge and **never `scrollWidth`** — an inline box reports 0, which is exactly the vacuous pass that let 758 nearly ship half-fixed.

- **(no build number — `api/abc.js` only, same session as 761–762)** · ABC Supply was calling a host that does not exist · The 401-then-fetch-failed thread from earlier the same session ended here: once the diagnostic fix (previous entry) turned "fetch failed" into a real answer, production said `Could not reach api.partners.abcsupply.com (ENOTFOUND: …)` — proof, not a guess, that the file's own guessed default host was simply wrong, confirmed the moment the auth host (a separate, always-correct host) stopped being the variable. Checked against **11 of ABC's own endpoint reference pages** on `apidocs.abcsupply.com` (branch, frequent/recent items, search, search-availability, pricing, order templates, search-branches, item availability, place/get orders) — all agreeing: real hosts are `partners.abcsupply.com` (production) / `partners-sb.abcsupply.com` (sandbox — a hyphenated suffix, not a subdomain prefix, unlike every other host in the file). **The host was only half of it.** 7 of the file's 9 data-action paths were ALSO missing their real `/api/{family}/v{n}` prefix — `/branches` should have been `/api/location/v1/branches`, `/orderTemplates` should have been `/api/order/v2/orders/templates`, and so on; only `frequents`/`recents` already happened to be right. Fixing the host alone would have swapped one dead end for a wave of fresh 404s on the very next attempt. `priceItems`'s request body was a third, separate defect: this file invented `items[]`/`unitOfMeasure`/`variation`, none of which exist in ABC's real schema (`shipToNumber`/`branchNumber`/`purpose`/`lines[]`, confirmed against ABC's own verbatim example JSON, including the required `purpose` enum `estimating|quoting|ordering`). All three fixed together, proven with a harness that mocks `fetch` to **record** the exact URL/method/body each of the 9 actions sends rather than simulate success — 9/9 match ABC's documented values exactly, and the identical harness run against the pre-fix file (the one just merged in #271) goes 9/9 red, reproducing the wrong host on every single action including the two whose paths were already correct. `searchItems`/`priceItems` response-*parsing* on the client side is explicitly NOT verified by this fix — still best-guess field names, flagged in OPEN_ITEMS as the next thing to check once a real 200 comes back.

- **(no build number — `api/abc.js` only, same session)** · ABC's 400 was explaining itself and nobody could hear it · The routing fix landed and worked: production stopped failing at DNS and started getting real answers from the real host (`ABC GET /api/product/v1/items/2153354-2/frequents -> HTTP 400` — ABC's server, not a network error). But the 400 arrived with **no reason attached**, because the reason was being dropped one layer short of the screen: `abc()` parked ABC's parsed error body on `err.detail`, the handler dutifully returned it as a separate `detail` field, and `index.html`'s `api()` reads **only** `j.error` — so `detail` was constructed, transmitted, and discarded on arrival. **The exact same class as the bare "fetch failed" defect earlier the same session** (`e.cause` discarded), which is the second time in one session that this file has thrown away the answer it already had. `abcReason()` now folds the body into the message string the UI actually renders, covering the REST shapes that exist in the wild (`{message}`, `{errors:[{message}]}`, `{errors:[{code}]}`, `{error:"…"}`, RFC7807 `{title,detail}`) with a raw-JSON and raw-text fallback so an unknown shape degrades to "show me everything" rather than silently matching nothing; `detail` still travels intact. 8/8 green, **7 red on the pre-fix file** (every shape rendering as a bare `-> HTTP 400`). ⚠️ **Deliberately NOT changed in the same build**: the documented-optional query params (`itemsPerPage`/`pageNumber`/`branchNumber`) were left alone so the next attempt tests ONE variable. Two account formats have now been tried against Theo's real account and both 400 — `2153354-2` (from `account.abcsupply.com`, matching the single-digit-suffix examples throughout ABC's docs) and bare `2153354`; the invoice renders the same account a third way, `2153354-0001`. **A third guess would have been the wrong move** — ABC has been stating the reason all along.

- **763** · ABC Supply reaches the real catalog — three stacked faults, each invisible until the one in front of it was fixed · **(1)** The host did not exist (ENOTFOUND, fixed in the previous entry). **(2)** With the host right, ABC answered `Bad Request: Required query parameter pageNumber not specified` on frequents/recents — a parameter **ABC's own documentation lists as Optional**. Only readable at all because the same session had just shipped `abcReason()`; before that it was a bare `-> HTTP 400`. `pageQs()` now sends `pageNumber` + `itemsPerPage` always and `branchNumber` when the caller has one (genuinely optional — it enriches each row with that yard's availability). **Trust the measured error over the published doc.** **(3)** Underneath both, two more invented dialects that would each have surfaced as a fresh mystery: `searchItems` sent `{query, branchNumbers, page, pageSize}` and **not one of those fields exists** — ABC takes `filters:[{key,condition,values}]` + `pagination:{itemsPerPage,pageNumber}`, and the only key that matches free text is `itemDescription`, which is also why the availability-first ladder is **deleted rather than reordered**: `/search/availability/items` accepts only `itemNumber`/`branchNumber`, so it could never have served the catalog box. And `priceItems` POSTed to the correct path but the CLIENT parsed `j.items`/`j.prices` when ABC returns **`lines[]`** carrying **`unitPrice`** — `arr` was therefore *always* empty and every price fell through to "Branch will price — call them": a **plausible-looking wrong answer on a money surface**, the worst kind. Plus `uoms:[{name,code}]` on search rows vs a flat `uom` string on frequents rows, only the latter handled. ⚠️ **Two deliberate non-decisions**: `embed:['branches']` instead of a `branchNumber` *filter* (a filter drops every item that yard does not stock — a narrowing call that needs real data, not a guess), and a single-token miss retried as `itemNumber equals` (Theo works from invoices full of codes) while a multi-word miss is not. Gates: `check_build` green (762→763, marker + negative control); request-shape harness **18/18 green, 9 red** on the pre-fix file, asserting against ABC's published examples rather than against itself.

- **764** · ABC's rejection is readable — **three faults in a single line of code** · Pricing came back 401 and the screen showed `ABC POST /api/pricing/v2/prices -&gt; HTTP 401 — This user is n`, cut off exactly where the reason begins. All three faults were in one `catch` line: **(a) `esc()` then `.textContent` DOUBLE-ESCAPES** — `textContent` escapes by definition, so pre-escaping renders the entity literally, which is why an arrow printed as `-&gt;`; **(b) `.slice(0, 60)`** truncated ABC's sentence at the point where it stops being a status and starts being an explanation; **(c)** it wrote into `.pr`, which is `float:right; max-width:120px` — a message column about three words wide. Fixed with a `.prmsg` line at full item width that wraps, cleared on each retry, `:empty{display:none}` so it costs nothing when there is no error. **This is the FOURTH time in one session that this feature discarded the answer it already had** (`e.cause` → `err.detail` → this), and the first three each cost a build to rediscover. `gate_764.mjs`: **7/7 green, 6 red on 763** — Chromium rather than jsdom because two of the three faults are layout and text-encoding, which jsdom cannot judge. ⚠️ **The gate's own negative control caught a vacuous pass in the gate**: "nothing is clipped" read `!undefined` on the pre-fix build, where the element does not exist, and therefore passed on a build with no message element at all — now requires the element first. The project's own warning, earned again in the harness rather than the app.

- **765** · Find my Ship-To — stop guessing account numbers, ask ABC · 764 made the refusal readable and it named itself immediately: *"not authorized to view pricing data for the provided shipTo number, **0003**. Please try a different shipTo number."* `0003` is the sequence printed on an invoice, **not** ABC's identifier — the identical trap as the bill-to, where the invoice said `2153354-0001`, the myABCsupply portal said `2153354-2`, and the API wanted a third form (`2153354-1`). **A fourth guess was the wrong move**, so `search-accounts` is now wired: `POST /api/account/v1/search/accounts` filtered to `accountType=Ship-to`, which returns the ship-tos this key may actually price against — ABC's own example numbers are independent 7-digit values (`1163698`), nothing derivable from the bill-to. The picker shows **name + address**, because a rep knows the JOB, not the number, and tapping a row writes the value into the field *and* the saved config. **This is the shape every account field on this screen should have had from the start.** `gate_765.mjs`: **10/10 green, 9 red on 764**, driving the real sequence end to end — reproduce the 401 on `0003`, list, tap, then assert the FOLLOW-UP price request body carries the real number and renders `$72.00`. Asserting on the sent body is the point: a picker that looks right but never reaches pricing passes a DOM-only check and fails this one. ⚠️ **The control CRASHED on its first run** (bare `.click()` on a button 764 does not have) — BUG_CLASSES 37 again; every interaction is guarded now, because a control that dies proves nothing.

- **✅ ABC Supply WORKS — a real branch price, 13 Aug 2026** · `$76.00` on 11IWRRGU2, Ship-To `2153354-2` / Bill-To `2153354-1` / Branch `106`. **The last fault was not code at all**: `2153354-2` is the number printed on `account.abcsupply.com`, it 401'd earlier when tried as a *bill-to*, and that made it look invalid — it was simply in the wrong field. Both suffixes belong to the same base account and are not interchangeable. **Before calling an ABC account number wrong, try it in the other box.** Six faults in total, each invisible until the one in front of it was fixed: nonexistent host → missing path prefixes → a required parameter the docs call optional → invented request fields in search AND a wrong response field in pricing → an error message mangled three ways so nothing could be read → a ship-to display code mistaken for an identifier. **The through-line worth carrying forward: this feature threw away the answer it already had four separate times** (`e.cause`, `err.detail`, the 60-char truncation, and finally a value sitting in the wrong input). After the first fix, every single answer came from reading ABC's own words — the docs were wrong twice (`pageNumber` "optional", the host), and ABC's live error text was right every time.

- **(no build number — `spark/` only, 13 Aug 2026)** · **The AccuLynx migration ran for the first time, and the pipeline could not have completed one** · Built, harnessed and merged on 11 Aug without ever touching the real API; gates 1–2 have now been run against Cardinal's live account and turned up **five faults**, each of which alone would have wrecked the import. **(1)** `/jobs` was paged with `recordStartIndex`, **a parameter that does not exist** — and AccuLynx does not reject an unknown query parameter, it answers `200` and returns page one, forever. So a misspelling was indistinguishable from broken pagination, which is exactly how the day-one probe read it ("the pagination unit is NOT a record offset here"); the unit assumption had been right all along and the name was wrong. Measured: `startIndex`, `page` and `offset` are silently ignored too. **(2)** `pageSize` asked for 100 against a **hard cap of 25** (`400 "Page Size must not be greater than 25."`), and the cap is inconsistent per endpoint — `/jobs` and `/custom-fields` refuse 26 while `/contacts`, `/milestone-history` and `/representatives` allow it, so 25 is the only value every route takes. **(3)** The site address arrives as `locationAddress` (with `street1`, and `state` as an object carrying `abbreviation`); `dig_address()` looked only at `address`/`jobSiteAddress`/`streetAddress1`, so **all 166 clients imported with a BLANK address** — which also silently disabled duplicate detection, because `find_collision()` matches on the street number, making the first dry run's headline "0 collisions" an artifact of the bug rather than a finding (the corrected run finds **2 real ones**). **(4)** `/jobs/{id}/representatives` returns its `user` as an unexpanded `{id,_link}` ref with no email — the same trap the code already handled for `/contacts` via `?includes=` — so **every client landed on the admin** instead of the 6 real reps; fixed by resolving against `/users` in one call. **(5)** That fallback was **silent**, because the "rep not on roster" warning keyed off a display name that was also empty on an unresolved ref: 166 misassigned clients and a clean review file. ⚠️ **Both offline harnesses were GREEN through all five**, because their fixtures were **invented rather than observed** — the push fixture used `detail.address.streetAddress1` and a pre-filled `sales_owner.user.email`, the fetch stub read `recordStartIndex`. A stub written from the implementation's own mental model encodes that model's mistakes and cannot disagree with it; this is class 15 moved up a level, and it is now `BUG_CLASSES.md` **45** (the silently-ignored parameter and its unexpanded-ref cousin are **44**). Fixtures are now transcribed from real responses with the date, and every new assertion is negative-controlled against the pre-fix code — the existing scenarios never exercised the offset at all, because two fixture items fit inside one 100-row page. Sub-resources were also reading the API's default page of **10** with no pagination; they now ask for 25 and report loudly if a `count` still outruns one page. **Result: 166 records fetched, 0 failures; files a confirmed NO-GO** (all six candidate read routes 404 on every job, exactly as the public docs predicted). Dry run after the fixes — driven through the Supabase connector with every write path stubbed to raise, a substitute for gate 3 and explicitly not a replacement — reports **164 new · 2 collisions · 0 unmappable · 0 warnings · PO 1044–1207**, reps spread nick 42 / theo 39 / jerry 35 / joey 29 / jacob 18 / curtis 3, 7 jobs carrying insurance data for Phase C. **Nothing written to Cardinal.** ⛔ Blocked on one thing: `CARDINAL_PASSWORD` is stale (`400 invalid_credentials`; the email is correct and neither variable has stray whitespace) — refresh it and gates 3→4→5 run as written. Two decisions waiting on Theo: the 2 collisions (Karrie Johnson 804 E Center St, Dan Thompson 2825 Arden Ave — both already in Cardinal, default is attach not duplicate) and **two AccuLynx test records** (`test test`, `Team Test`, both at 5735 Webster Street) that would otherwise import as clients.

- **(no build number — `spark/` docs only, 13 Aug 2026)** · **Gate 3 passed for real, and the notes turned out to be gone as well** · The dry run re-run from Theo's own Windows desktop **matched the Supabase-connector replay exactly** (34 clients / max PO 1043 / 10 roster emails / 164 new / 2 collisions / 0 unmappable, every stage count identical), which retroactively validates the substitute gate. The stale `CARDINAL_PASSWORD` was only ever the cloud environment's copy — **the password itself was always correct**, and `auth.users.last_sign_in_at` had already proved the account healthy hours before the wrong value was identified by its shape (15 chars, starts and ends with a symbol, contains a `!`). Worth keeping: `push_acculynx.py` reads **only** `CARDINAL_EMAIL`/`CARDINAL_PASSWORD` — never the AccuLynx key, which is the credentials fence working as designed, and it meant the desktop route needed one secret rather than two. **The find of the session came from one question from Theo — "What about notes?"** `lead.notes` is empty on all 166 imports because `map_job()` reads `detail.description`/`detail.notes` and neither key exists on this tenant — superficially the same defect as the blank address, but **this one cannot be fixed by re-pointing the mapping, because there is nothing to point it at**: measured **806 job messages across 156 of the 166 jobs (94%)**, with twelve endpoint spellings all answering 404 (`/notes`, `/messages`, `/comments`, `/job-messages`, `/conversations`, `/posts`, top-level collections filtered by `jobId`), no v1 or v3, and no swagger/OpenAPI spec served. `/jobs/{id}/history` DOES answer — 6,191 actions — but records only *that* a note happened (`"Job Message Added"`, with date and author) and never the text; `custom_fields` is a single `Policy Number` on all 166 rows with **zero** values. So notes sit behind the same upload-and-audit fence as files, and the two are now one decision. **✅ SETTLED (Theo): front door only.** He read the terms and ruled out a scraping/browser-automation pass — correctly, and **rate-limiting does not move an automated bulk extraction out of the restricted category**; the stronger argument is that tripping AccuLynx's security flags would LOCK the account and destroy the only copy of those messages mid-migration. ⚠️ **The runbook had previously RECOMMENDED exactly that browser pass — that text is now corrected in the runbook, `OPEN_ITEMS.md` and `HANDOFF.md`. Do not propose it again.** Permitted routes recorded in order: an offboarding data-export request; **asking for written permission** (the restriction is contractual, so the counterparty can waive it, and a departing customer is often granted it — a yes makes a properly rate-limited fetcher legitimate); asking whether another API tier exposes message/file reads; and AccuLynx's own Reports/CSV exports, which are sanctioned by definition. The manual fallback was scoped rather than left as a scary 806: live work is 61 jobs / 378 messages and the realistic target is the **41 Approved jobs = 249 messages**, since the 81 Prospects carrying 317 messages mostly never became work. ⛔ **Do not cancel the AccuLynx subscription until this is settled** — same trap already recorded for CompanyCam, where the bytes die with the account.

schedules on the Schedule Board, which writes `appointments` kind `job` — it reads that now, preferring the
next build day, falling back to the most recent past one. Checklist keys stay last in the chain (additive,
not a swap). Also: `checklist.materials_ordered_at` + Mark ordered in the Materials tab, and closed
punch-outs pushed into `buildActivityEvents()`. `punch_steps.sql` ships (steps + template columns).

`window.CardinalProduction`, same hideAllViews/navSetView/scroll-lock/observer registrations. Three panes:
home (five boxes + week strip + the day), cal (full month, named chips, Needs-a-date queue), list. Back goes
up ONE level. No floating buttons. Cardinal Steel, dark base + scoped light twin.

outcome line. `CardinalPunchProfile.openItem` routed into the card.
